beginner.summary: For Java developers and test engineers who can write Java classes but have written few unit tests; this is a Java unit testing course built around Mockito, not a course on Mockito alone. Covers JUnit Jupiter (the JUnit 5 programming model, now released as JUnit 6.1), AssertJ and Mockito 5: test structure and assertions, Maven and Gradle builds, creating, stubbing and verifying mocks, matchers, @InjectMocks, the MockitoExtension, spies, exceptions, BDDMockito, captors, test reports and debugging, ending with a tested service layer.
prerequisites: Writes Java classes, interfaces, collections and exceptions at the level of a Java SE 17 or 21 course
Uses an IDE such as IntelliJ IDEA or Eclipse and runs Maven or Gradle commands from a terminal
Has a laptop with JDK 21 or 25, Git and rights to download dependencies from Maven Central
outcomes: Set up Maven and Gradle builds that run JUnit Jupiter, AssertJ and Mockito tests on JDK 21 or later
Write readable unit tests with clear arrange, act and assert steps, JUnit and AssertJ assertions and names that describe behaviour
Replace collaborators with mocks and spies, stub return values and exceptions, and verify interactions with matchers and captors
Read Surefire, Gradle and IDE reports, diagnose failing tests and avoid the mistakes that make mock-based tests brittle
